JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation due to death of Eranna in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners is as follows:-
That on 16-05-2025 at about 4-00 pm.

Eranna was riding XL Super bearing Reg.No.KA-52-Q-8434 near Yedehalli U turn Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk,
Bengaluru and in order to enter Bangalore - Tumkuru NH-48, he was standing with the vehicle by the side of U Turn, at that time the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.TN-28-AE-6472 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit his vehicle against the motorcycle of Eranna which was standing near the U turn result of which he fell down with the motorcycle and the front right wheel of the lorry ran over the vehicle of Eranna result of which Eranna sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the hospital.
The petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies.
3. Prior to the accident, Eranna was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 48 years.
He was working at private Company and earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the untimely death of Eranna, petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony.
4. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Lorry bearing Reg.TN-28-AE-6472 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. Respondent no.2 /the Insurer of Lorry bearing Reg.TN-28-AE-6472 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license and that the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.

It is further contended that the deceased being the rider of the motorcycle was not holding valid driving license and he was not wearing helmet, hence Eranna had also contributed Nagarathnamma vs Rajkumar N R on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16137854/
2 negligence.
6.

On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Eranna succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 16-05-2025 at about 4-00 pm.,
near Yedehalli U turn, Sonpura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District,
Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.TN- 28-AE-6472?
2.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order
or Award ?
7. The petitioner No.1 got examined herself as Pw1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

Petitioners have categorically contended that on 16-05-2025 at about 4-00 pm.,
when Eranna (hereinafter called the deceased) was riding XL Super bearing Reg.No.KA-52-Q-8434 near Yedehalli U turn Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru and in order to enter Bangalore - Tumkuru NH-48, he was standing with the vehicle by the side of the road, at that time the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.TN-28-AE- 6472 (hereinafter referred as to the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the offending vehicle against the motorcycle which was standing near the U turn result of which deceased fell down with the motorcycle and the front right wheel of the lorry ran over the vehicle of Eranna, further result of which Eranna sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the hospital.
11.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 12 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, Sketch, Inquest report, PM report and death summary, Statement of Nagarathnamma vs Rajkumar N R on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16137854/
3 witness, notice u/sec.133 IMV Act two in numbers, reply notice two in numbers, IMV report, charge sheet, etc., are the material documents to prove the present issue.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Timmappa GH, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 0192/2025 of Nelamangala Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b) of B.N.S

The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 281, 106 of B.N.S.
13.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the spot of accident is on the edge of the road near U turn.
It is not in dispute that offending vehicle was proceeding from Tumkuru- Bangalore National Highway.
The deceased was riding the motorcycle from Somapura Industrial Area and in order to enter Bangalore - Tumkuru Highway he was standing with the motorcycle on the U turn.

The driver of the offending vehicle by driving the vehicle on the Tumkuru - Bangalore National Highway took the vehicle on the edge of the road where deceased was standing with his vehicle near the U turn and hit to the vehicle of the deceased.
Hence, from the topography of the scene of occurrence it can be said that rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Admittedly, respondent no.1 and 2 have not adduced oral evidence.

If really accident in question has occurred in the manner other than the one stated by the petitioners,
then definately the respondents would have adduced the evidence either of the driver of offending vehicle or any of the eye witness to the accident.

Hence, materials placed on record clearly and clinchingly proves the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle in which deceased has not contributed any amount of negligence.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in Affirmative.
14. Issue no 2 :
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it can be said that deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
It is stated that at the time of accident deceased was aged about 48 years.
In this regard, petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P11 which reflects the date of birth of deceased as 01-01- 1977.
As the accident in question has taken place in the year 2025, it can be said that deceased was aged about 48 years as on the date of accident.
15. It is contended by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner no.2 and 3 being the son and daughter of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.
As per the own evidence of the PW.1, petitioner no.2 and 3 are doing collie work and petitioner no.3 is her married daughter who is residing in her matrimonial house.

If the age of the petitioner no.2 and 3 shown in the cause title is concerned, as per the own case of the petitioners, petitioner no.2 is aged about 23 years and petitioner no.3 is aged about 20 years and she is married.

Hence, it can be said that petitioner no.2 and 3 though are the legal representative of the deceased and though are entitled to file claim petition but they are not the dependents of the deceased and they were not depending on the income of the deceased.
Hence, it can be said that petitioner no.1 being the wife of the deceased alone is the dependent of the deceased.

So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was working in Private Company and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the actual income and avocation of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident in question has occurred in the year 2025, court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.17,000/- per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.17,000/- p.m.
17.

Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, and she alone is the dependant of the deceased,  of the annual income is to be deducted towards personal expenses and remaining  is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

18. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case as the deceased was 48 years, 25% should be added towards future prospects.

19. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.17,000/-, if 25% is added towards the future prospect it comes around Rs.21,250/-, out of it if 1/2 is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.10,625/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 46 to 50 years is '13.
Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.16,57,500/- (Rs.10,625/- x 13 x 12 = Rs.16,57,500/-).
20. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost her husband and petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their father.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned, slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

21. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Nagarathnamma vs Rajkumar N R on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16137854/
5

Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.

22. From the medical document produced by the petitioners it can be gathered that from 16-05-2025 till 19-05-2025, the deceased was taking treatment as an inpatient and on 19-05-2025 he breathed his last.
The petitioners have produced 13 medical bills issued from Mytri Multi Speciality Hospital, Bangalore for Rs.2,89,047/- as per Ex.P10.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.2,89,047/- towards the medical expenses.

23. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
2 Transportation and funeral Rs. 18,150/-
expenses 3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs. 1,45,200/-
parental
consortium
4 Loss of Dependency Rs. 16,57,500/- 5

Medical expenses Rs.
2,89,047/-
 Total Rs. 21,28,047/-
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.21,28,047/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
24. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the findings on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
25. Issue No.4:- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 1 to 3 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.

ORDER  The claim petition filed by the Nagarathnamma vs Rajkumar N R on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16137854/
6 petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs..21,28,047 + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on IA No.I.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.21,28,547/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Twenty Eight Thousand Five Hundred Forty Seven only).
A Sum of Rs.21,28,047/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the amount along with interest within 2 months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.20,31,747/- Petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.48,400/- Petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.48,400/-

Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner on proper identification.
So far as the amount apportioned to the petitioners no 2 and 3 are concerned same is ordered to be released in their favour after due identification through E -payment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
